# Singapore start-up Ropedia raises US$22 mil in pre-Series A round for robot-training data The robotics data company has raised US$30 million so far, and will use the latest funds to gather more training data, increase device production and expand in Singapore and the US\. Ropedia, a Singapore start-up that supplies training data for robots and physical artificial intelligence systems, has raised US$22 million \($28\.4 million\) in a pre-Series A funding round\. It did not identify the investors in the latest round, saying only that it was led by venture firms with experience in AI, deep technology and infrastructure in Southeast Asia\. The deal brings its total funding to US$30 million\. An earlier round included investors and individuals connected to Google, Andreessen Horowitz, Nvidia and Amazon, according to the company\. Ropedia's proprietary wearable devices record first-person video, depth, movement and audio as people carry out physical tasks\. The company processes that information into training material for developers seeking to teach robots how to perform tasks in real-world settings\. # India’s FinTech Rises Globally as Bengaluru Claims Nearly 70% of Total Funding Written By: Reviewed By: Published on: 12 Aug 2026, 1:54 pm Updated on: 12 Aug 2026, 1:54 pm ### **Overview** - India’s fintech sector raised over $2\.2 billion across 100-plus funding rounds\. - Late-stage fintechs received more than 70% of total H1 funding\. - Bengaluru dominated funding, while Accel emerged as the most active investor\. India’s fintech sector continued to attract strong investor interest in the first half of 2026, even as funding decisions became more selective\. The sector raised more than $2\.2 billion across 100-plus funding rounds, marking the strongest half-year funding performance since H1 2023\. The latest numbers come as global venture capital remains cautious following the funding peak of 2021\. For India, the H1 2026 performance points to continued investor confidence, but also shows a market where larger, established fintech companies are attracting a greater share of capital\.
